title: Conditional entropy chain and disjoint-block bounds

items.title: Conditional entropy chain and disjoint-block bounds
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_m$ be standard-Borel spaces, let $Q_i$ be probability measures on $X_i$, and let $P$ be a probability on $\prod_{i=1}^mX_i$. Write $P_i$ for its $i$th marginal and use the directional extended relative entropy $D(\cdot\Vert\cdot)$ of [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Then
$$D(P\Vert Q_1\otimes\cdots\otimes Q_m)\geq\sum_{i=1}^mD(P_i\Vert Q_i).$$
If the left side is finite, the conditional chain rule gives the stronger equality
$$D(P\Vert\textstyle\bigotimes_iQ_i)=D(P_1\Vert Q_1)+\sum_{i=2}^m E_P\,D(P_{X_i\mid X_1,\ldots,X_{i-1}}\Vert Q_i),$$
and each conditional increment is at least $D(P_i\Vert Q_i)$. If the left side is infinite, the displayed inequality is understood in the extended order and is automatic. This applies to finitely many disjoint spatial blocks after their particle counts and positions have been fixed; zero-occupancy blocks contribute zero.

items.title: Gaussian mark normalization, moments, and exponential controls
Measurable information contraction and Pinsker bound
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on a measurable space and let $T$ be a measurable map to another measurable space. Then
$$D(T_*P\Vert T_*Q)\leq D(P\Vert Q),\qquad \|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}:=\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|\leq\sqrt{D(P\Vert Q)/2}.$$
The entropy convention is the directional KL definition of [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]], and the total-variation convention is the event-supremum convention of [[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]]. The inequality remains valid when $D=+\infty$.

items.title: Interacting marked phase-space and reference measures
items.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $d\geq1$ and let $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ be the numerical even Borel pair potential. Assume the stability, cell-superstability, lower-regularity, and decreasing-integrable-tail conditions of [[def-csm-stable-superstable-continuum-interaction]], with its fixed cell side $\ell$, and the superstable regular interaction, unit-coordinate, and periodic-image conventions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. These are model hypotheses; the definitions do not prove that a particular material satisfies them. Use the finite-region phase-space and statistical-state conventions of [[def-csm-statistical-state-observable]].

Let $E_0>0$ joules be the energy unit, $\ell_0>0$ metres the length unit, $m>0$ kilograms the particle mass, and $p_*>0$ kg m s$^{-1}$ the momentum reference. Positions $x=q/\ell_0$ are dimensionless numerical coordinates; write $V_L=L^d$ for numerical volume. The dimensionless positional energy $U_{L,bc}$ is the physical pair energy divided by $E_0$, with $bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}$ and the exact image convention above. If $T>0$ kelvin, put $\beta_{\rm phys}=1/(k_BT)$ in J$^{-1}$ and $b=\beta_{\rm phys}E_0=E_0/(k_BT)>0$.

Let $Q_L$ be the unit-intensity Poisson probability on positional configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, defined by [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. Its $N$-particle conditional law $Q_{L,N}$ is uniform on the unordered simple $N$-point configurations; in labelled coordinates it is $L^{-dN}dx_1\cdots dx_N$ on the no-collision set. On an $N$-point configuration, attach one momentum $p_x\in\mathbb R^d$ to each point and use the symmetric product reference $r^{\otimes q}$ with $r(dp)=dp/p_*^d$. The finite phase reference is
$$R_{L,N}(dq,dp):=Q_L(dq)\,r^{\otimes q}(dp)\,1_{\{N(q)=N\}}.$$
It is sigma-finite; the factor $e^{-V_L}/N!$ from the Poisson sector is retained. In physical coordinates the corresponding one-particle product scale is $h_{\rm ref}^d=\ell_0^dp_*^d$, an action to the power $d$; it is a reference convention, not a derived quantum constant.

For a marked configuration define the total dimensionless energy
$$\mathcal H_{L,bc}(q,p)=U_{L,bc}(q)+\sum_{x\in q}K(p_x),\qquad K(p)=\frac{|p|^2}{2mE_0}.$$
For $b>0$, [[lem-csm-gaussian-mark-moments]] gives $\kappa_b=\int e^{-bK}r(dp)=(2\pi mE_0/(bp_*^2))^{d/2}$ and the probability kernel $\nu_b(dp)=\kappa_b^{-1}e^{-bK(p)}r(dp)$. Whenever the positional canonical partition is finite and positive, nonnegative product integration [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] gives exact identities
$$Z^{\rm ph}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b)=\int e^{-b\mathcal H_{L,bc}}dR_{L,N}=\kappa_b^N Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b),\qquad C^{\rm ph}_{L,N,bc}=C^{\rm pos}_{L,N,bc}\,\nu_b^{\otimes q}.$$
Here $Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}=E_{Q_L}[1_{\{N(q)=N\}}e^{-bU_{L,bc}}]$ and the canonical probabilities are the normalized respective integrands. Under a full grand preparation of activity $z_{\rm ph}$, integrating each momentum changes the positional activity to $z=z_{\rm ph}\kappa_b$; thus a positional activity $z=e^\alpha$ corresponds to $z_{\rm ph}=e^\alpha/\kappa_b$. These are exact definitions and normalizations; they do not assert dynamical equilibration or finite-volume grand convergence. For periodic boundary conditions, simultaneous translation of all positions modulo the period preserves $R_{L,N}$ and $\mathcal H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$: the conditional position law is uniform on the torus, the mark reference is invariant under relabelling points, and the image energy depends only on pair displacements. Hence normalized canonical and finite band restrictions are torus-translation invariant.

items.title: Marked periodic continuation and local restriction
items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be the positional configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. The **marked configuration space** $\Omega^{\rm mark}$ consists of marked point sets $\xi\subseteq\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ with spatial projection $q=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\exists p\in\mathbb R^d,\ (x,p)\in\xi\}$ that is simple and locally finite, and with exactly one mark $p_x$ paired to each $x\in q$. Its sigma-algebra is generated by the marked counts $N_{A\times C}(\xi)=\#\{(x,p)\in\xi:x\in A,\ p\in C\}$ for bounded Borel $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and Borel $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$. The positional projection is $\pi(\xi)=q\in\Omega$. For a bounded Borel set $\Delta$, the **marked local restriction** is $\xi_\Delta=\{(x,p)\in\xi:x\in\Delta\}$ with the induced count sigma-algebra; write $N_\Delta(\xi)=\#\xi_\Delta$. A **marked-local observable on $\Delta$** is a real measurable function of $\xi_\Delta$; it is bounded when its supremum norm is finite.

Let $d\geq1$, $L>0$, and $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$. A finite marked configuration consists of a finite simple set of positions $q\subseteq\Lambda_L$ and a mark map $p:q\to\mathbb R^d$, as in [[def-csm-full-marked-model]]. Its **marked periodic continuation** is
$$\omega^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,q,p}:=\{(x+Lk,p_x):x\in q,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}.$$
The spatial positions in this set are distinct: if $x+Lk=y+Lj$ for $x,y\in[0,L)^d$, then coordinatewise $x-y=L(j-k)$ forces $j=k$ and $x=y$. Every bounded spatial region meets finitely many lattice translates of the finite set $q$, so the continuation has a locally finite spatial projection.

For a bounded Borel set $\Delta\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, define its **marked local restriction** by
$$\omega^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,q,p}|_\Delta:=\{(y,p_x)\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,q,p}:y\in\Delta\}.$$
This is an element of $\Omega^{\rm mark}$, with the induced sigma-algebra of marked counts above. If $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda_L$, the restriction is exactly the original marked points with positions in $\Delta$.

items.title: Existence of the independent Gaussian-marked positional lift
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $P$ be any probability law on the simple locally finite positional configuration space $\Omega$ of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], and let $
u$ be a probability on the momentum mark space $\mathbb R^d$. Use the marked configuration space $\Omega^{m mark}$ and local restrictions $\xi_\Delta$ of [[def-csm-marked-periodic-continuation]]. Define translations by $T_yq=\{x+y:x\in q\}$ and $T_y^{m mark}\xi=\{(x+y,p):(x,p)\in\xi\}$. Then there is a unique probability law $P^{m mark}$ on $\Omega^{m mark}$ whose positional projection is $P$ and whose marks, conditional on the entire positional configuration, are independent with common law $
u$. If $P$ is translation invariant, meaning $(T_y)_\#P=P$ for every $y\in\mathbb R^d$, then $(T_y^{m mark})_\#P^{m mark}=P^{m mark}$ for every $y$. For the Gaussian $
u_b$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], this is the independent Gaussian-marked positional lift. This is a mathematical marking construction, not a physical preparation or a convergence result.

items.title: Total-energy concentration and controlled canonical windows
items.statement:
Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Use the model and dimensionless energy $\mathcal H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]]. Let $L_n\to\infty$, $V_n=L_n^d$, and integers $N_n$ satisfy $N_n/V_n\to\rho>0$, where $\rho$ is an interior attainable density for the positional canonical rate. Fix $b>0$. Assume $F_b(\rho)$ is the periodic exact-particle log-partition rate supplied by [[thm-tdmath-periodic-fixed-n-limit]] for every $b'$ in a neighborhood of $b$, and is differentiable at $b$. Write $C_n^{\rm ph}$ for the full fixed-$N_n$ canonical law, and define
$$e_b(\rho)=-\partial_bF_b(\rho)+\frac{d\rho}{2b}.$$
Then, for each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, there exist $c_\varepsilon>0$ and $n_0$ such that
$$C_n^{\rm ph}\!\left(\left|\mathcal H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e_b(\rho)\right|>\varepsilon\right)\le 2e^{-c_\varepsilon V_n}\quad(n\ge n_0).$$
Consequently there is a nonincreasing sequence $\delta_n\downarrow0$ for which the full phase band
$$A_n=\{N=N_n,\ |\mathcal H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e_b(\rho)|\le\delta_n\}$$
has $C_n^{\rm ph}(A_n)\to1$. It has positive finite phase-reference measure for all sufficiently large $n$. This constructs a controlled shrinking window; it makes no claim about every prescribed shell width or an exact energy surface.

items.title: Classical full-phase interacting ensemble preparations
items.statement:
Fix the model, physical reference conventions, mass, potential and energy window specified by [[def-csm-full-marked-model]] and [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]]. Identify the action reference a_0 of [[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]] with h_ref=ℓ_0p_* from the marked model. Adopt the following alternative preparations whenever their normalizations are finite and positive:

1. At fixed exact particle number $N$, controls and $T>0$, use the canonical density proportional to $e^{-\beta H}$ relative to the declared phase reference, as in [[post-csm-canonical-preparation]].
2. For a sequence satisfying all hypotheses of [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]]—including AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, HB, an interior attainable density, the periodic exact-particle log-rate hypothesis near $b$, and differentiability at $b$—at fixed exact $N_n$ use the uniform full-phase reference law restricted to its constructed band $A_n$. “Uniform” means normalized restriction of that finite reference measure; it is an energy-window preparation, not a zero-width surface measure. This postulate makes no existence claim for that specific band when those theorem hypotheses fail.
3. For particle exchange, use the countable-sector grand preparation of [[post-csm-grand-preparation]]. Its full dimensionless activity is the fugacity $z_{\rm ph}:=e^{\beta_{\rm phys}\mu}>0$, where $\beta_{\rm phys}=1/(k_BT)$ in J$^{-1}$ and the chemical potential $\mu$ is in J per particle. When matching positional activity $z=e^\alpha$ at inverse temperature $b$, choose $z_{\rm ph}=z/\kappa_b$, as in [[def-csm-full-marked-model]].

These laws are adopted statistical preparations. They do not follow from Hamiltonian energy conservation, do not assert that any isolated dynamics reaches these distributions, and do not encode an experimental observation. The band sequence is the particular controlled shrinking window constructed conditionally by [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]].
items.physical_scope: Adopted classical massive-particle preparations for a specified superstable regular pair model; no assertion of dynamical equilibration, measured accuracy, or finite-volume grand convergence.

items.title: Full uniform phase shell has vanishing specific canonical KL
items.statement: Assume AC and the hypotheses and notation of [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]]. Let $R_n=R_{L_n,N_n}$ be the finite phase reference of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], let $A_n$ be the constructed band, and set $M_n^{\rm ph}(E)=R_n(E\cap A_n)/R_n(A_n)$. Let $C_n^{\rm ph}$ be the full fixed-$N_n$ canonical probability. Then $D_n=D(M_n^{\rm ph}\Vert C_n^{\rm ph})$ satisfies $D_n/V_n\to0$. This is a mathematical statement about a normalized measure restriction; it does not assert $D_n\to0$ or global total-variation convergence.

items.title: Full phase shell marginal satisfies the positional variational bound
items.statement:
Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC and HB, the exact superstable regular pair interaction and periodic-image convention of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], and integer side lengths $L_n\to\infty$ with exact particle numbers $N_n/V_n\to\rho>0$ at an interior attainable density. Fix $b>0$. Assume the positional canonical log rate is $F_b(\rho)$, and choose finite $\alpha$ with
$$P_{\rm Leb}(α,b)=F_b(ρ)+αρ,$$
where $P_{\rm Leb}$ is the grand pressure per numerical volume with Lebesgue $1/N!$ normalization. Let the positional grand variational minimizer of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]] at activity $\exp(\alpha)$ and inverse temperature $b$ be the singleton $\{P_*\}$. Let $R_n=R_{L_n,N_n}$ be the phase reference of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], let $A_n$ be the band of [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]], set $M_n^{\rm ph}(E)=R_n(E\cap A_n)/R_n(A_n)$, and let $B_n$ be its positional marginal. For any local-tame test $f$, write $B_n[f]=E_{B_n}f(\omega^{(L_n)})$ and $C_n^{\rm pos}[f]=E_{C_n^{\rm pos}}f(\omega^{(L_n)})$, where $\omega^{(L_n)}$ is the periodic continuation. Let $\bar B_n$ be the barycenter of $R_{L_n,\omega}$ under $B_n$. Then $\bar B_n$ converges to $P_*$ in $\tau_L$, equivalently $B_n[f]\to P_*(f)$ for every local-tame $f$; also $C_n^{\rm pos}[f]\to P_*(f)$ for every such $f$. The periodized empirical fields of the exact-$N_n$ canonical laws converge in probability in $\tau_L$ to $P_*$ by [[thm-tdmath-periodic-fixed-n-limit]], and $P_*$ has intensity $\rho$. Here $P_*$ is an infinite-volume positional variational state; no finite-volume grand-canonical local convergence or DLR identification is asserted.

items.title: Spatial random-occupation conditional mark entropy bound
items.statement:
Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[thm-csm-full-shell-positional-minimizer]]. Let $M_n^{\rm ph}$ be the normalized phase-reference restriction to $A_n$, and let $B_n$ be its positional marginal. Given the full position configuration $q$, let $b_{n,A}(\cdot|q)$ be the shell conditional law of marks on the marked local restriction of [[def-csm-marked-periodic-continuation]]. By torus translation invariance, represent any bounded Borel region $\Delta$ by a fixed translate inside $\Lambda_{L_n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Choose an axis-parallel half-open cube $C\supseteq\Delta$ of side $\ell>0$, independent of $n$, and pack $L_n^{\rm pack}=\lfloor L_n/\ell\rfloor^d$ disjoint translates of $C$ into the periodic cube, so $L_n^{\rm pack}/V_n\to1/|C|$. For the independent Gaussian mark reference $\nu_b$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]],
$$E_{B_n}D(b_{n,\Delta}(\cdot|q)||\nu_b^{\otimes N_\Delta(q)})\leq D(M_n^{\rm ph}||C_n^{\rm ph})/L_n^{\rm pack}.$$
Thus the left side tends to zero. When $\Delta$ itself is an axis-parallel half-open cube, take $C=\Delta$ to obtain the stated packing rate $1/|\Delta|$. Occupancy $N_\Delta(q)$ is random; the comparison is for the full spatially selected set of particles, not a fixed set of labels.

items.title: Full interacting shell, canonical, and variational-grand local marked equivalence
items.statement:
Assume AC and the hypotheses and notation of [[thm-csm-full-shell-positional-minimizer]], including its AC, ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB assumptions. Fix a bounded Borel region $\Delta$ and use the marked periodic continuation and local restriction defined in [[def-csm-marked-periodic-continuation]]. By translating $\Delta$ and the spatial argument of $G$ together, take a representative with $\Delta\subseteq[0,\infty)^d$; then $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda_{L_n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. This translation preserves the expectations because the finite laws are torus-translation invariant and the limiting independent mark lift of the stationary positional state is stationary. Let $M_n^{\rm ph}$ be the uniform full-phase band law, $C_n^{\rm ph}$ the exact-$N_n$ full canonical law, and $P_*$ the singleton positional grand variational minimizer. Give points of $P_*$ independent marks with kernel $\nu_b$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], and denote the resulting infinite marked law by $P_*^{\rm mark}$, whose existence is supplied by [[lem-csm-gaussian-marked-lift-existence]]. For finite-volume expectations, evaluate $G$ on the restriction $\omega^{\rm per}_{L_n,q,p}|_\Delta$; under $P_*^{\rm mark}$, evaluate it on $\xi_\Delta$. Then for every bounded marked-local observable $G$ on $\Delta$ in the sense of [[def-csm-marked-periodic-continuation]],
$$E_{M_n^{ph}}G\to E_{P_*^{mark}}G,\qquad E_{C_n^{ph}}G\to E_{P_*^{mark}}G.$$
The matched full grand activity is $\exp(\alpha)/\kappa_b$ by the normalization identity in [[def-csm-full-marked-model]]; $P_*^{\rm mark}$ is the independent-Gaussian marked lift associated with that positional variational minimizer. If additionally $|G|\leq C(1+N_\Delta)$, shell convergence also holds for $G$. This is fixed-region convergence, not uniform over growing regions or arbitrary unbounded momentum observables. No finite-volume grand-canonical convergence or DLR converse is asserted.

items.title: Local kinetic energy and first and second momentum expectations
items.statement:
Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[thm-csm-local-mark-kl-bound]]. Fix a bounded half-open cube $\Delta\subseteq[0,\infty)^d$; then $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda_{L_n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. By torus translation invariance this placement gives the same limits as any fixed translate of the cube. Let $N_\Delta(q)=\#(q\cap\Delta)$. For $b>0$ and $K(p)=|p|^2/(2mE_0)$, the full shell law satisfies
$$E_{M_n^{ph}}\sum_{x\in q\cap\Delta}K(p_x)\to dρ|Δ|/(2b),\quad E_{M_n^{ph}}\sum_{x\in q\cap\Delta}p_{x,i}\to0,$$
$$E_{M_n^{ph}}\sum_{x\in q\cap\Delta}p_{x,i}p_{x,j}\to(mE_0ρ|Δ|/b)\delta_{ij}.$$
The corresponding canonical and marked variational-grand laws have the same limits by their independent Gaussian marking. Momentum is in kg m s^-1, E_0K is in joules, and b=E_0/(k_BT) is dimensionless. These conclusions concern only the named moments, not every unbounded mark observable.

items.title: Physical interacting local phase-space ensemble bridge
items.statement: Under the hypotheses and adopted preparations below, shell and exact-N canonical expectations of every fixed bounded marked-local observable converge to the same Gaussian-marked positional variational state. The shell also has the kinetic-energy, first-momentum and second-momentum expectation limits stated in [[thm-csm-local-momentum-moments]]. This is a conditional deduction from the model assumptions, not an observation or an equilibration claim.
items.physical_scope: Conditional predictions for fixed marked local observables and the named momentum moments in the adopted classical preparation model; no equilibration, experiment, material fit, finite-volume grand limit, or universal shell-width claim.

title: Conditional entropy chain and disjoint-block bounds — Examples

items.title: Energy concentration without local equivalence
items.statement: Fix $0<\theta<1$ and $\epsilon>0$. The refuted claim is: every sequence of laws $A_N$ on $\{0,1\}^N$ for the reference energy $H_N(x)=\epsilon\sum_i x_i$ whose energy density converges deterministically to $\epsilon\theta$ has first-coordinate marginals converging in event-supremum total variation to the Bernoulli-$\theta$ first-coordinate marginal of the product reference. Use $\|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}=\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|$. This is a finite-model claim, not an experimental assertion.

items.title: Small entropy density without homogeneous local convergence
items.statement: Assume AC. Fix $0<\theta<1$ and $\epsilon>0$, and let $P_N,H_N$ be the reference and energy of [[cex-csm-energy-concentration-not-local]]. The refuted implication is: for every sequence of laws $Q_N\ll P_N$, if $N^{-1}D(Q_N\Vert P_N)\to0$, $H_N/N\to\epsilon\theta$ in $Q_N$-probability, and $N^{-1}H_{\rm Sh}(Q_N)\to h(\theta)$, then the first-coordinate marginal of $Q_N$ converges in event-supremum total variation to Bernoulli$(\theta)$. Here $H_{\rm Sh}(Q_N)=-\sum_xQ_N(x)\log Q_N(x)$ and $h(\theta)=-\theta\log\theta-(1-\theta)\log(1-\theta)$ use natural logarithms.
